contract: POST /api/upload accepts the upload page's multipart form (library, folder, title, author and series for books, files) from a user with upload permission and writes each file into <folder>/<author>/<series>/<title>/ for a book library or <folder>/<title>/ for a podcast library, sanitizing each part. It answers 200 and creates no library item by itself.

Mapping only: no tests executed in this invocation. Historical evidence is retained for provenance and does not verify this checkout; named tests are assertion leads, not exhaustive proof of every stated requirement.
force is not applicable: the route has no force, hard or override parameter; a repeated upload overwrites the destination derived from the title and file name.

invariants.contract: Rejections come in the source order: 401 without a token; 403 when the user cannot upload, before the body is read; 400 without a file or without string library, folder and title; 404 for an unknown library; 403 when the user cannot access the library (404 still wins for an unknown library); 404 when the folder is not one of the library folders. A rejected upload writes no file or directory and changes no row.
exceptions: Named tests listed are relevant package-level current tests; their assertions do not yet prove every route branch or the complete upstream contract.

invariants.contract: A successful upload writes each file with its exact bytes below <folder>/<author>/<series>/<title>/ for a book library (absent author or series are skipped) and below <folder>/<title>/ for a podcast library, creating the directories; the title is sanitized (":" becomes " - ") and the directory part of a file name is dropped by the multipart parser. The response is 200 and the upload creates no library item synchronously; a later upload of the same title with a series goes to its own directory and leaves the earlier files.
exceptions: Named tests listed are relevant package-level current tests; their assertions do not yet prove every route branch or the complete upstream contract.

invariants.contract: Uploading the same title and file name twice answers 200 both times and leaves one file at the same path with the second content (the move overwrites), with no duplicate directory or file.
exceptions: Current test names are discovery anchors; repeated-operation outputs need explicit assertion mapping.
